note: The refute-repo control: 36 claims about six repo files, pinned at one commit of main. ANSWER KEY: every claim carries its label. No arm is given this file's path, and `score` reports any agent whose commands or reads name it. Ids are opaque and shuffled; do not reintroduce a speaking id.

claims.claim: When usageRecords in ledger.mjs sees one message.id on several transcript lines, it keeps the usage from the first of those lines and counts the later ones as repeats.
claims.label: refuted
claims.why: Line 77 counts the repeat, then line 78 sets the entry unconditionally, so each later line overwrites the earlier one: the last line's usage is kept.

claims.claim: The ci workflow runs on pushes to three branches, main, changeset-release/main and staging, and on pull_request events with no branch filter.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Line 13 is the push filter; line 14 is a bare pull_request trigger.

claims.claim: In .claude/settings.json the subagent-stop-guard hook is registered under the Stop event, with matcher "*".
claims.label: refuted
claims.shape: field given to the wrong event
claims.why: The event is SubagentStop, not Stop. The matcher is right.

claims.claim: In fleet-nightly.yml the 'Dispatch the nightlies in order' step has a 290-minute timeout, 10 minutes shorter than its job's 300 minutes.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Both numbers are on the cited lines.

claims.claim: In score.mjs the `string` kind drops punctuation, as the `text` kind does.
claims.label: refuted
claims.why: The string pipeline is dashes, whitespace and casefold; punctuation is only in text and name.

claims.claim: EFFORTS in arms.mjs lists exactly five values: low, medium, high, xhigh and max.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Line 2.

claims.claim: When the build and the tests leave the working tree dirty, the ci workflow's build job fails.
claims.label: untested
claims.why: The step is written to exit 1 on a dirty tree, so no line contradicts the claim; only a run settles it.

claims.claim: The deny list in .claude/settings.json blocks `gh secret` commands.
claims.label: refuted
claims.shape: field given to the wrong list
claims.why: `gh secret` is in the ask list (lines 40-56), which closes the deny list at line 39.

claims.claim: fleet-nightly runs every day at 02:17 by its cron schedule, and can also be started by hand with workflow_dispatch.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Line 5 is the cron; line 6 is workflow_dispatch.

claims.claim: ledger.mjs applies Haiku 5.5's long-prompt card only when a request's uncached input tokens alone exceed 100,000; cache reads and cache writes do not count toward that threshold.
claims.label: refuted
claims.why: The threshold is compared against input plus cache read plus cache write.

claims.claim: In score.mjs the `name` kind removes a leading title followed by whitespace, such as "Dr. " or "Mr. ", before it folds case and drops punctuation.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: titlePrefix is the first step of the name pipeline.

claims.claim: ci.yml's browser-install step tries `playwright install` up to 3 times and gives each attempt 600 seconds.
claims.label: refuted

decides.text: timeout 300 pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium

claims.why: Three attempts is right; each is given 300 seconds.

claims.claim: An arm id may start with a hyphen, provided every character in it is a lowercase letter, a digit or a hyphen.
claims.label: refuted
claims.why: The first character must be a letter or a digit.

claims.claim: In .claude/settings.json the cloud-session-setup hook is a SessionStart hook with matcher `startup|resume` and a 900-second timeout.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Both are in the entry that runs cloud-session-setup.sh, inside the SessionStart array that opens at line 73.

claims.claim: fleet-nightly's step that opens or updates the 'Nightly conductor failing' issue runs whenever the job fails, on whatever branch the run was started from.
claims.label: refuted
claims.why: The step runs only on main.

claims.claim: Of the six `pnpm verify` gate steps in ci.yml, `pnpm typecheck` runs before `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm test:dist` runs last.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Lines 77-82 in order.

claims.claim: When a usage record's cache write carries no 5-minute/1-hour split, ledger.mjs counts the unsplit tokens as 5-minute writes.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Line 34 computes the unsplit part and line 40 adds it to cw5m.

claims.claim: normalise("0x10", "number") in score.mjs returns "16".
claims.label: refuted
claims.why: "0x10" does not match NUMBER, so line 41 returns "NaN:0x10".

claims.claim: Exactly one hook in .claude/settings.json sets a timeout, and that timeout is 600 seconds.
claims.label: refuted
claims.why: One hook sets a timeout, and it is 900.

claims.claim: fleet-nightly's concurrency group does not cancel a run that is already in progress.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Line 21.

claims.claim: validateArm in arms.mjs reports 'has no effort' only when the effort field is undefined; an effort of null or the empty string is reported instead as not one of the allowed values.
claims.label: refuted
claims.why: null and the empty string take the 'has no effort' branch too.

claims.claim: In ci.yml the `changeset-release/main` branch filter sits on the pull_request trigger, not on the push trigger.
claims.label: refuted
claims.shape: field given to the wrong event
claims.why: The filter is under push (line 4); pull_request at line 14 has none.

claims.claim: In ledger.mjs a 1-hour cache write on Opus 5.5 is priced at $8 per million tokens, against $5 for a 5-minute write.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Line 5.

claims.claim: In .claude/settings.json the orphaned-agents-report hook runs at SessionStart on the `startup` and `resume` matchers.
claims.label: refuted
claims.shape: field given to the wrong hook
claims.why: Its matcher is resume|compact; startup|resume belongs to the two hooks after it.

claims.claim: The `only` input of fleet-nightly defaults to `fleet-smoke`.
claims.label: refuted
claims.why: The default is the empty string, meaning all nightlies; fleet-smoke is only the description's example.

claims.claim: The `number` kind in score.mjs accepts a leading plus sign, so the string "+5" normalises to "5".
claims.label: refuted
claims.why: The pattern allows only an optional minus sign.

claims.claim: ci.yml gives its build job a 35-minute timeout, and gives the browser-install step its own 20-minute timeout.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Lines 19 and 54.

claims.claim: validateArms in arms.mjs rejects an arm whose id is exactly `gold`, and an arm whose id starts with `referee`.
claims.label: confirmed

decides.text: if (arms.some((a) => a && a.id === "gold")) errors.push('arm id "gold" is reserved');

claims.why: Lines 35 and 37.

claims.claim: The sandbox in .claude/settings.json excludes `gh *` and `git *` commands.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Both are in excludedCommands, which opens at line 138.

claims.claim: fleet-nightly's `force` input is a boolean that defaults to false, and when set it dispatches even a nightly the conductor already dispatched on main in the last 24 hours.
claims.label: refuted

decides.text: already dispatched on main in the last 12 h

claims.why: The window is 12 hours. The type and default are right.

claims.claim: usageRecords in ledger.mjs records an assistant usage line that has a message.id but no `effort` field under the effort `(unset)`.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Line 81.

claims.claim: Calling normalise in score.mjs as normalise("x", "date"), with no custom kinds, throws an error.
claims.label: untested
claims.why: "date" is not a set: kind, a custom kind, number, boolean or file, and PIPELINES has no "date", so line 53 throws. The code is consistent with the claim; a behaviour claim takes untested unless a line contradicts it. (The first wording, "a kind that has no pipeline", was refuted by number, boolean and file: review before the run.)

claims.claim: In ci.yml `pnpm build` runs before `pnpm check:match-harness-snapshots`.
claims.label: refuted
claims.why: The snapshot check is line 79, the build line 80.

claims.claim: The deny list in .claude/settings.json covers `git push --force-with-lease` as well as `git push --force` and `git push -f`.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.why: Lines 28-30, inside deny.

claims.label: refuted
